reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it directs viewers to connect and fund a wallet before deploying and activating a front-running bot, linking that funding to automated token trading and claimed returns. It promotes a reported 50x result and claims of up to 1000 BNB per day, although the records do not independently verify the contract's operation or any resulting gain.

follow the description of the video As far as downloading Metamask and also funding it. Make sure that it's connected to the Binance Smart Chain
the next step in this process is just funding your contract which is simple enough, you just go to your wallet
The action button then engages all the Constructors that I built in as far as engaging the Pancake Router. It automatically buys and sells for you.
automatically sell within a minute

opening.argument: The material contains concrete limitations, costs, and conditions rather than presenting an unconditional financial promise. It expressly says the contract is for Binance Smart Chain and will not work on Ethereum mainnet, and it warns that users may need enough funds for gas and burn fees. The description also says the bot targets tokens with a maximum burn fee, while the speaker describes returns as something that may occur after automated trading. Those qualifications support a risk-aware technical demonstration, not a representation that every viewer will profit.

citations.quote: This contract have been designed for Binance Smart Chain (BEP20) and won't work with Ethereum mainnet.
I got messages from people who didn't fund enough to cover gas fees and possible burn fees.
Bot targets token contracts with max 10% burn fee and anything lower.
I can almost guarantee that I got something back by now

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited funding and trading instructions establish what the demonstration does, but not that the speaker concealed risk or guaranteed a result. The description identifies network incompatibility and warns about gas and burn fees. The prosecution's excerpts also do not show that viewers were promised a fixed return, protected from loss, or told that the method worked on every token.

citations.quote: won't work with Ethereum mainnet
didn't fund enough to cover gas fees and possible burn fees
So you'll only be competing with other bots on the mempool

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The limitations concern network compatibility and the amount needed to cover fees; they do not warn that the claimed strategy may fail or that deposited funds may be lost. More importantly, the speaker reports an apparent 50x result and then says viewers could have upwards of 1000 BNB a day. Those highly favorable claims overwhelm the narrower technical qualifications.

citations.quote: It's already around 50x.
You know you could have upwards of 1000 BNB a day
I've had really good luck with this. The last few weeks I've made you know, several hundred BNB.

opening.argument: The primary presentation is a hands-on programming and deployment tutorial. Its title calls it a tutorial, and the narration walks through creating a file, copying contract information, compiling it in Remix, connecting a wallet, and deploying the contract. The supplied frames likewise show a development environment with source code, compiler controls, deployment controls, and a blockchain address page. That is consistent with teaching an operational blockchain workflow; the presence of an asserted outcome does not change the central instructional format.

citations.quote: Trading bot Front running Bot Tutorial for Pancakeswap Updated No Downloads
I'm going to be building our contract, so you can pause this video if you need time.
So we're going to deploy this to our wallet.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats ordinary tutorial steps as proof of a scam. Connecting Remix, compiling code, deploying a contract, and checking an address are technical operations visible in the walkthrough. Even the cited automatic trading statement describes the intended function of the code; it does not establish that the video is an endorsement of a fraudulent service rather than a demonstration of how the mechanism is presented.

citations.quote: Then you just follow over to Remix.
Let me go compile FrontrunBot.
now we have our deployment utility right here

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling something a tutorial does not make it merely educational when the tutorial tells viewers to fund the deployed contract and activate it. The speaker does not just explain source code: he sends funds, presses the action function, and presents the resulting return as evidence. The instructional format therefore serves a practical profit solicitation rather than neutral programming education.

citations.quote: the next step in this process is just funding your contract
we will just go over here and press the action button
It's already around 50x.

opening.argument: The evidence is better characterized as a software and blockchain operations demonstration than as a conventional deposit scheme. The sources describe contract code, PancakeSwap routing, a wallet connection, and a function called Action. They do not show a request for passwords or private keys, a downline or referral structure, or a contractual guarantee of repayment. The description also identifies the supported network and links ordinary tools such as MetaMask and Remix. Whatever one thinks of the trading strategy, the supplied material does not establish those additional scam mechanisms.

citations.quote: we're going to copy the contract information that I put in the description
There's also the pancake router for Pancake swap version 2
MetaMask Download: https://metamask.io/download.html
Access Remix: https://remix.ethereum.org/

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's evidence shows a viewer funding a contract and invoking an automated function, but that is also what a blockchain software demonstration would require. It does not show that the creator takes custody of the wallet, asks for credentials, recruits participants, or promises repayment independent of trading. The phrase about buying and selling describes software behavior, not proof that the creator operates a deceptive payment mechanism.

citations.quote: we're going to send some funds to that contract
The action button then engages all the Constructors that I built in
It automatically buys and sells for you.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing mechanisms are not necessary to establish this type of scam. The relevant mechanism is the instruction to transfer funds into a deployed contract, activate it, and expect rapid automated profit. The speaker specifically says the system returns 90% of purported profit to the wallet and claims a 50x result, while the record provides no independent confirmation that any gain occurred.
